      "maxMarks": 4,
      "answer": "The student's difficulty is due to context-dependent forgetting. This is explained by the encoding specificity principle, which states that memory is improved when the context at retrieval matches the context at encoding. The student practised in her usual study room, so the environmental cues (e.g., sights, sounds) were part of the encoding. When she tries to recall in a different room, the mismatch in context reduces retrieval cues, making recall harder. This demonstrates that forgetting can be caused by a lack of appropriate retrieval cues, not necessarily a failure of storage.",
